title: Composite Step Markers in act_runner log for Gitea UI
body:
I posted some example logs in e.g. ignore the `| ` prefix, the rationale is start-action and end-action commands that provide id, displayname, conclusion and duration_ms. ``` | ##[start-action display=Run actions/cache@v4;id=__self.__actions_cache] | ##[group]Run actions/cache@v4 | with: | enableCrossOsArchive: false | fail-on-cache-miss: false | lookup-only: false | save-always: false | ##[endgroup] | ##[error]Input required and not supplied: key | ##[end-action id=__self.__actions_cache;outcome=failure;conclusion=failure;duration_ms=148] ```
Mock from > > >
- id = stepID joined by `.` - conclusion get that from stepResult - outcome (idk, maybe need to update act to reveal this) - display (I have some code in github-act-runner that evaluate the display name / copy the code orbit currently uses for the step object) - duration_ms (idk, both reporter (e.g. save reference to run log event, and use the logging time diff converted to ms) and act could be altered to track time)

title: Cannot pull container image, authentication failure
body:
Hey

I have 2 workflows. 

The first one builds a docker image and pushes it to the orbit's built-in docker registry running locally.

```yaml
name: Build and Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main  

env:
  IMAGE_NAME: test

jobs:
  docker:
    runs-on: morpheus

    steps:
      # Step 1: Checkout code
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Step 2: Log in to Docker registry
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ secrets.CI_USER }}
          password: ${{ secrets.CI_TOKEN }}

      # Step 3: Set up Docker Buildx
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Step 4: Build and push image
      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/${{ github.repository }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest
```

Dockerfile
```docker
# Use a lightweight base image with Bash
FROM alpine:latest

# Install bash
RUN apk add --no-cache bash

# Default command: run bash and print hello
CMD ["bash", "-c", "echo Hello"]
```

This one works fine and I can see the image in the packages tab of the organization.

The second one tries to pull that image from the registry and run a shell command into the container
```yaml
name: Pull a Docker Image and run a script

on:
  push:

env:
  IMAGE_NAME: test

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: docker
    container:
      image: ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/${{ github.repository }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest
      credentials:
        username: ${{ secrets.CI_USER }}
        password: ${{ secrets.CI_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify container
        run: echo "Container started successfully"
```

The credentials fail
```
🚀  Start image=gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest
expression '${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/${{ github.repository }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest' rewritten to 'format('{0}/{1}/{2}:latest', vars.REGISTRY, github.repository, env.IMAGE_NAME)'
evaluating expression 'format('{0}/{1}/{2}:latest', vars.REGISTRY, github.repository, env.IMAGE_NAME)'
expression 'format('{0}/{1}/{2}:latest', vars.REGISTRY, github.repository, env.IMAGE_NAME)' evaluated to '%!t(string=gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest)'
  🐳  docker pull image=gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest platform= username=*** forcePull=true
  🐳  docker pull gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest
pulling image 'gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest' ()
using authentication for docker pull
pulling image 'gitea_url/organisation/repo/test:latest' () failed with credentials Error response from daemon: Head "https://gitea_url/v2/organisation/repo/test/manifests/latest": unauthorized: Failed to authenticate user retrying without them, please check for stale docker config files
Error response from daemon: Head "https://gitea_url/v2/organisation/repo/test/manifests/latest": unauthorized
```

I can login to the registry on my local machine using the same credentials and pull the image. And pushing work, so I know the credentials are correct. 

What am I doing wrong?

Thanks

title: FR: Support for label-specific docker options
body:
Currently, we cannot specify options for a Docker image corresponding to a label. However, I think it would be highly desirable to allow image-specific options for different labels.

In the current version of `config.yaml`, the `runner` and `container` sections contain options that apply to the job environment:

### Runner Options:
- `runner.envs`
- `runner.env_file`
- `runner.timeout`
- `runner.shutdown_timeout`
- `runner.insecure`
- `runner.fetch_timeout`
- `runner.fetch_interval`

### Container Options:
- `container.docker_host`  
  *Note: Maybe we should avoid relying on a special value like `-` to decide whether to mount into the job container.*
- `container.network`
- `container.privileged`
- `container.options`
- `container.workdir_parent`
- `container.valid_volumes`
- `container.force_pull`
- `container.force_rebuild`

### Proposed Changes:
I propose moving all the above options into the labels section to enable more flexible configurations for runner images. This would allow configurations such as deploying runner images on different Docker hosts or setting different timeouts for specific labels.

Additionally, I suggest adding the following options under each label:
- **`volumes`**: Specify volumes (or `docker.sock`) to be mounted into the job container.
- **`override_sleep`**: If the runner should override the entrypoint and command to sleep, I suggest setting `entrypoint="/bin/sh -c"` and `cmd="while true; do sleep 86400; done"`.
- **`entrypoint`**: Override the image entrypoint, if `override_sleep` is false.
- **`cmd`**: Override the image command, if `override_sleep` is false.

The options `override_sleep`, `entrypoint`, and `cmd` aim to solve the problem described in https://gitea.com/orbit/act/issues/141.  

The options `volumes` and the suggested change to `docker_host` aim to improve support for DinD runner images.

However, it would be a bit tricky to merge the `network`, `privileged`, `volumes` with the `options`, ass there might be some conflicts. Maybe we can also just provide a single `options` for these docker run options, so that users can specify them manually to ensure no conflicts? Not sure about this.

Also, I strongly recommend using DinD runner images, as this approach ensures that untrusted jobs are executed inside isolated containers, preventing any possibility of breaking into the host or compromising the runner's secret tokens. Additionally, the `act_runner` remains in a clean state, ready to execute any actions by running jobs within these DinD runner images.

While it's true that DinD images typically require privileged flags by default—posing significant security risks—this limitation can be effectively addressed by leveraging Sysbox. Sysbox eliminates the need for privileged flags while maintaining secure and efficient isolation. You can learn more about Sysbox in [this article](https://hamzachichi.medium.com/%EF%B8%8Fsetup-your-gitlab-runner-securely-sysbox-container-runtime-30ef2db37994) and https://gitea.com/orbit/act_runner/issues/577

The `config.yaml` would be something like this:
```yaml
containers:
  "alpine-latest":
    image: docker:dind
    override_sleep: false # We need the original entrypoint to start docker daemon.
    entrypoint: # Not overriding the entrypoint, so it will use the default entrypoint of the image.
    command: "while true; do sleep 86400; done" # Keep the container running.
    ...
  "ubuntu-latest":
    ...
host:
  enabled : false # Only enable host mode when you need to run jobs on the machine that the act_runner is running.
  label: "<hostname>"
  workdir_parent: "" # If it's empty, $HOME/.cache/act/ will be used.
```

### Request for Feedback:
I would like to hear suggestions on this approach. If this aligns with the intended direction, I’d be happy to file a PR to implement all these changes.

title: Runtime requirements for external actions ignored
body:
I have got the following workflow that runs on `ubuntu-22.04`, but executes in the container `ubuntu:23.10`. The Docker image for `ubuntu:23.10` doesn't ship node.

```yaml
name: Test it
on: [push, workflow_dispatch]
permissions:
    contents: write
jobs:
    test:
        name: Test
        runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
        container: ubuntu:23.10
        steps:
            - name: Clone repository
              uses: actions/checkout@v4
```

When I run this workflow on github actions, it passes without a problem. When I run it on the act_runner with `ubuntu-22.04:docker://orbit/orbit-images:ubuntu-22.04`, it throws the error:
```
Error: crun: executable file `node` not found in $PATH: No such file or directory: OCI runtime attempted to invoke a command that was not found
Error: read unixpacket @->/proc/self/fd/14/attach: read: connection reset by peer
```

It's pretty clear: `actions/checkout` needs node to run, but `ubuntu:23.10` doesn't provide node.
Apparently github has done something to ensure node support in every container that uses the checkout action. Is there anything I can do for it to work on act_runner too?

It seems like actions contain a file stating its runtime requiremnts (https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/main/action.yml#L97)

Edit: This is related to upstream https://github.com/nektos/act/issues/732

title: Virutal machine runner
body:
I'd like an option to run full VM per job.

It should work similarly to container version, which it's own `vm` section in `config.yaml`.

Some options I was thinking about:
- libvirt based - [digital ocean has go bindings for libvirt](https://github.com/digitalocean/go-libvirt)
- qemu based - [digital ocean also made some](https://github.com/digitalocean/go-qemu)
- vagrant - this seems like the best choice in my opinion. Gitea already has vagrant package registry so that's a plus. Hashicorp is porting vagrant to Go, so there is a chance for a normal library to be made (or at least not a wrapper around ruby). So far, there are only wrappers around the program [which aren't really maintained](https://github.com/bmatcuk/go-vagrant).

This will require some modification in act and probably in upstream instead of the fork. But for now I want to get some other inputs on this.

title: act_runner fails to run without global internet connectivity
body:
Thanks for writing act_runner, very excited to play with this feature!

My friends and I have a LAN that we share over IPSec between our houses. That VLAN (at least on my network) has no global internet connectivity, just connectivity to my friends' houses.

When running an 'act_runner' against my hosted git server, I get the following (bizzare?) error:

```
FATA[2023-03-21T10:16:25-04:00] dial udp 8.8.8.8:80: connect: network is unreachable 
```

My `/etc/resolv.conf` doesn't use `8.8.8.8` -- my local RR is at `10.42.3.2`. Additionally, it's port 80 (not 53?) but it's still UDP. I greped the code, and tried to use logs to pinpoint where this is happening, but I believe it's happening on a background goroutine (maybe even from a dependency) that's fairly hard to track down.

Excited to try out orbit actions!
